summary: Two-story NPS lookout cab on Elk Mountain in Glacier NP; built 1930-32, burned or razed in 1965; a concrete foundation remains.

facts.status_note: Burned or razed by the Park Service in 1965 (1963 on one site); a concrete foundation and cable remain.

access.note: Reached by a hike in Glacier National Park; no tower stands at the site.

visit.trail_note: About 6.8 miles round trip from a footpath that starts at a parking area; the route crosses private land before the railroad tracks south of the park boundary.

events.note: NPS report: a trail to the summit and a temporary lookout; two new lookouts installed that year, one on Elk Mountain near Fielding Ranger Station.
Two-story cab under construction in 1932 (WillhiteWeb); Montana History Portal record gives 1932 as the build year.
Last used in 1959, per a 2019 hike description.
Burned by the Park Service on May 27, 1965 (WillhiteWeb, Forest Lookouts) or razed by the NPS that year (Roaming Bear). Firelookout.com gives 1963.

evidence.supports: Elk Mountain lies in the southern part of Glacier NP, west of Marias Pass.
evidence.quote: Elk Mountain (7,835 feet) rises in the southern part of Glacier National Park west of Marias Pass.

evidence.supports: Two-story NPS cab, dated 1930 on this site.
1930 NPS report: trail to the summit and a temporary lookout.
evidence.quote: There has been a trail built to the summit of Elk Mountain and a temporary lookout built there.

evidence.supports: Two new lookouts installed in 1930, one on Elk Mountain near Fielding Ranger Station.
evidence.quote: Two new lookouts have been installed this year -- one on Elk Mountain near Fielding Ranger Station.
May 27, 1965: The lookout was burned by the Park Service.
In 1932, the Elk Mountain lookout was under construction, a 2-story cab.

evidence.supports: Burned by the Park Service on May 27, 1965.
evidence.quote: In 1965, the lookout was burned by the Park Service on May 27.
The lookout was built in 1932 and destroyed in 1965.

evidence.supports: Last used in 1959; razed by the Park Service in 1965.
evidence.quote: It was built in the 1930s, last used in 1959, and razed by the National Park Service in 1965.

evidence.supports: Concrete foundation with rusty bolts and cable marks the former lookout site.
evidence.quote: An old concrete foundation with rusty bolts sticking out and strands of cable lying about mark the location of the former fire lookout.
This hike is 6.8 miles round trip with an elevation gain of 3,373 feet.

evidence.supports: Footpath starts at a parking area.
evidence.quote: A footpath heads north from the parking area and intersects an old road at 0.8-miles.

evidence.supports: Route crosses private land before the railroad tracks south of the park boundary.
evidence.quote: The route passes through private land before reaching the railroad tracks south of the park boundary.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com dates the two-story NPS cab to 1930. The 1930 NPS report describes a temporary lookout and two new lookouts that year, while WillhiteWeb and the Montana History Portal record give 1932 for the two-story cab. The story reports both.
Firelookout.com gives 1963. The other four sources give 1965, so the story uses 1965 and notes the 1963 date.

notes_for_editor: Do not confuse with the NHLR Elk Mountain Lookout (US 1504, MT 82, Lincoln County, Kootenai NF), a different tower. The 1930 vs 1932 build date and 1963 vs 1965 destruction date are unresolved; the NPS 1930 report was read only as quoted by Forest Lookouts. The photo record says copyright not specified; check before reuse.
